requirement_text:
Functional Requirements

5. Functional requirements
5.1. Transferring Assets
5.1.1. Within the same department: data base can be updated directly without any request
5.1.2. Inter departments: request must be approved by a DA group member and faculty group member unless it came from a higher level group
5.1.3. Inter faculties transfer: request can be made by any authorised user and approved by faculty group or higher level
5.1.4. Transfer outside university should be approved by the university group

5.2. Editing Assets
5.2.1. Any administrative level user or inventory user can edit an asset that belongs to its department; same thing for faculty user, or university user; in order to make modification if he is authorised to do it.

5.3. Modifying assets
5.3.1. all fields of an edited asset can be modified except Ids
5.3.2. a bulk entry file can be used

5.4. Adding inventory assets
5.4.1. Any DA group member or authorised inventory group member asset is owned by the department
5.4.2. Any faculty member can add all related departments inventory
5.4.3. Any university group member can add all assets in the inventory
5.4.4. A bulk entry can be used to add many assets

5.5. Creating request to borrow an asset or a reserve a location
5.5.1. request can be made by any authorised user
5.5.2. After creation a request still pending waiting to be approved by an administrative level user according to that have this authority

5.6. Retuning assets
5.6.1. An inventory user should check returned asset and update inventory

5.7. Creating a new location
5.7.1. IT group members can create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level

5.8. Approving requests
5.8.1. Any administration level or authorised inventory group member can display all pending requests waiting for approval from this level and approve those requests
5.8.2. When request is treated user is notified by email
5.8.3. Request is added to the waiting for execution list
5.8.4. Inventory is updated when user receive requested asset

5.9. Authentication
5.9.1. Authentication is made by user name and a password for all users
5.9.2. administrative level working on administration computer

5.10. Changing permission
5.10.1. Any administrative level user can delegate another user to execute some or all his authorized actions. And this user acquires the role of inventory administrator

5.11. Output reports
5.11.1. Asset report by location
5.11.2. Request report
5.11.3. User permission user


Use case Scenarios

Name: Modify Use Case Identifier: MOD.UC Description
The use case describes the modification that the Inventory Admin can do.
Goal
The Inventory Admin initiates the use case. The use case presents all the modification
that can be done by the Inventory Admin.
Preconditions
1.   The Inventory Admin is authenticated

Assumptions
1.   We assume that use Knows the results of each operation there is no go back
actions
Basic Course
1.   Use case begins when Inventory Admin start searching for an asset
2.   Inventory Admin Edit the asset
3.   Inventory Admin modify asset properties

Alternate Course A:
Condition: administrator or authorised inventory user is working on waiting for approval
list or waiting for execution list
1.   Inventory user or Admin Edit the asset
2.   Inventory user or Admin modify asset properties

Exceptional Course :
1.
1. Inventory Admin search for asset
2. Inventory Admin edit asset
3. Inventory Admin asset out of inventory
4. Message error because asset cannot be modified
2.
1. Inventory Admin search for asset
2. Inventory Admin edit asset
3. Inventory Admin does not have sufficient privileges to edit asset
4. Message error is displayed
3.
1. Inventory Admin search for asset
2. no asset found
3. Message error is displayed

Post conditions
1.   The system state change according to modification
 
Actors
Inventory Admin, Inventory system, Authentication system

Included Use Cases
1.   Search use case
2.   Edit use case
3.   Authentication use case

Notes
We suppose that Hosting system and servers support all the operations

Name: Add New Asset Use Case

Identifier: ANI.UC
Description
The use case describes the operation of adding a new asset to the inventory.
Goal
The Inventory Admin initiates the use case. The use case presents how Inventory Admin
can add new inventory asset.
Preconditions
1.   The Inventory Admin is authenticated

Assumptions
1.   We assume that use Knows the results of each operation there is no go back
actions
Basic Course
1.   Use case begins when Administrator start a new asset
2.   Administrator select asset type
3.   Administrator select asset location
4.   Administrator select owner
5.   Administrator fill all asset properties

Alternate Course A: None

Exceptional Course:
1.   Use case begins when Administrator start a new asset
2.   Type does not exist in the list
3.   Administrator send exception request to IT to add the new type and the common properties

Post conditions
1.   Data base is updated
 
Actors
Inventory Admin, Inventory system, Authentication system
Included Use Cases
1.   Authentication use case

Notes
We suppose that Hosting system and servers support all the operations

Name: Create request Use Case 
Identifier: CRQ.UC Description
The use case describes the activity of creating a new request that the User can do.
Goal
The User initiates the use case. The use case presents request process that can be done by
User.
Preconditions
1.   The User is authenticated

Assumptions
1.   We assume that use Knows the results of each operation
2.   Only basic request form is available for level 0
3.   Requests forms provide search facilities to users levels 1, 2 and 3

Basic Course
1.   User select basic request form
2.   User type a small request text specifying asset (s) location,..
3.   User click on submit

Alternate Course A:
1.   User select advanced request form
2.   User enter asset serial number and location
3.   User enter small text describing operation to be done
4.   User click on submit

Alternate Course B:
1.   User select advanced request form
2.   User enter asset serial number and location
3.   User enter small text describing operation to be done
4.   User can add as many assets as he wants to the list by clicking add another asset button
5.   User click on submit



Alternate Course C:
1.   User select exception request form
2.   User enter a text message describing the exception that occurs
3.   User click on submit

Exceptional Course :
1. User search for asset
2. Asset not available to be borrowed
3. Error Message is displayed

Post conditions
A new request is pending waiting approval
Actors
Inventory Admin, Inventory system, Authentication system

Included Use Cases
1.   Search use case
2.   Authentication use case

Notes
We suppose that Hosting system and servers support all the operations

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers many core flows, but it has several semantic and control-flow gaps: request approval/update execution is incomplete, authentication/editing is overgeneralized, some required exception branches are missing, and there are a few unsupported behaviors. Previously noted granularity issues remain but are not repeated unless they still create a semantic defect.

defects.description: The approval flow does not model the required post-approval execution chain: once a request is treated, the user must be notified by email, the request must be added to the waiting-for-execution list, and inventory must be updated when the requested asset is received. The diagram only shows approval and an email step, with no waiting-for-execution state or inventory update tied to asset receipt.
defects.evidence: Requirements state: 'When request is treated, the user is notified by email' (R20), 'The request is added to the waiting for execution list' (R21), and 'Inventory is updated when the user receives the requested asset' (R22). Diagram nodes N39-N41 show display pending request list, approve request, and notify user by email, but there is no node or transition representing addition to the waiting-for-execution list or inventory update on receipt.
defects.suggested_action: Add the missing post-approval steps and connect them in order: approval -> add request to waiting-for-execution list -> notify by email -> execution/receipt event -> inventory update.

defects.description: The edit-asset flow only models a generic search/edit path and a privilege check, but it does not distinguish the required authorized actor classes and ownership constraint. The requirements allow administrative-level users, inventory users, faculty users, and university users to edit assets belonging to their department if authorized; this coverage is not represented explicitly and the privilege gate is attached only after a generic edit path.
defects.evidence: R6-R8 require that different authorized user categories can edit assets belonging to their department. The diagram uses one generic 'Search for asset' -> 'Edit asset' -> 'Modify asset properties' flow with a later 'Sufficient privileges?' decision, but does not represent the required role/department eligibility distinctions or the ownership condition.
defects.suggested_action: Model the authorized editor categories and the 'asset belongs to their department' condition before edit/modification, or otherwise encode the role/ownership checks explicitly in the decision logic.

defects.description: The modification requirement that all fields may be changed except IDs, and that a bulk entry file can be used, is not represented. The diagram only shows a generic 'Modify asset properties' step and no restriction on IDs or bulk-entry path.
defects.evidence: R9 says all fields of an edited asset can be modified except IDs; R10 says a bulk entry file can be used. The diagram contains only 'Modify asset properties' (N12) and 'Fill asset properties' (N23), with no explicit constraint on IDs and no bulk-entry alternative.
defects.suggested_action: Add a modification step that excludes IDs, and include an alternative branch for bulk-entry-file-based modification.

defects.description: The transfer flow does not cover the required approval rules for inter-faculty transfers and transfers outside the university. Inter-faculty transfer approval by faculty group or higher is modeled only as 'create transfer request' and 'approve transfer request' without the stated authority logic; outside-university transfer approval by the university group is shown as a direct approve step but without the explicit approval authority condition.
defects.evidence: R3 requires any authorised user to make inter-faculty transfer requests; R4 requires approval by faculty group or higher; R5 requires transfers outside university to be approved by the university group. The diagram has N58 'Create transfer request', N59 'Approve transfer request', and N60 'Approve transfer', but none of these nodes or decisions encode the required role conditions.
defects.suggested_action: Add explicit role-based approval decisions for inter-faculty and outside-university transfers, with branches for faculty-group-or-higher and university-group approval.

defects.description: The return-asset flow omits the required 'check returned asset and update inventory' behavior by an inventory user. The diagram has only a generic inventory-system check and update path, without the user role performing the check/update as specified.
defects.evidence: R17 requires that an inventory user should check the returned asset and update inventory. The diagram shows 'Check returned asset' and 'Update inventory' in the inventory system lane, not in the inventory user lane, and does not distinguish the user role executing these actions.
defects.suggested_action: Place the returned-asset check/update steps in the inventory-user lane or otherwise explicitly model the inventory user as the actor performing those actions.

defects.description: The exception-request path for creating a new location is incomplete. The requirement says IT group members create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level, but the diagram does not show IT as the actor receiving/processing that exception request, only the user sending it and then directly creating/modifying location structures.
defects.evidence: R18 requires IT group members to create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level. The diagram shows N25 'Send exception request' and then N26/N27 'Create new space'/'Modify floor structure' in the user lane, with no IT-group receipt or processing step.
defects.suggested_action: Add the IT-group member swimlane actions that receive the exception request and perform the location-creation/floor-structure modification.

defects.description: The diagram introduces an implicit requirement that authentication is only for a specific precondition set, but the requirements only state username/password authentication for all users. The additional linkage of authentication to multiple unrelated preconditions is not supported semantically.
defects.evidence: R23 only requires that authentication is made by user name and password for all users. The decision node N5 is annotated with many unrelated requirement tags (including edit, request, approval, change permissions, and authentication), which implies a broader semantic coupling than the requirement states.
defects.suggested_action: Keep authentication as a standalone username/password login step and avoid implying that it semantically governs unrelated business steps unless those links are explicitly required.

defects.description: The diagram adds an unsupported 'working on waiting for approval / waiting for execution list' condition as a gate for editing, but the requirements only mention this condition for an alternate course in the modify-use-case scenario and do not define it as a general prerequisite for editing assets. Using it as a generic privilege gate changes the meaning of the edit flow.
defects.evidence: R34-R35 describe an alternate course: an administrator or authorised inventory user working on the waiting-for-approval or waiting-for-execution list can edit/modify asset properties. In the diagram, N15 'Sufficient privileges?' is used as a generic gate after editing, which is a different and broader condition than the stated alternate course.
defects.suggested_action: Model the alternate-course condition only where it applies, and do not replace the specified privilege/working-list condition with a generic sufficiency check unless the requirement explicitly says so.

defects.description: The modify-use-case exceptional paths are only partially represented. The diagram shows a no-asset-found error and a generic insufficient-privileges error, but it does not represent the 'asset out of inventory' case as a distinct cause of modification failure.
defects.evidence: R36 requires an error when the asset is out of inventory; R37 requires an error for insufficient privileges; R38 requires an error when no asset is found. The diagram has a decision 'Asset found?' and a generic 'Sufficient privileges?' branch, but no distinct branch for 'asset out of inventory'.
defects.suggested_action: Add a separate decision or exception branch for 'asset out of inventory' so that it is not conflated with general missing-asset or privilege failures.

The same-department direct database update requirement is represented.
The add-new-asset flow includes the main creation steps and the exception path for an unknown type.
The diagram includes search, reporting, permission change, and several approval-related activities.

defects.description: Requirement R11 is not represented with a valid flow in the diagram.
defects.evidence: R11 requires that any DA group member or authorised inventory group member can add department-owned inventory assets. The diagram only shows a generic add-new-asset flow (N18-N24) initiated by 'User' / 'User selects asset type' and never models the DA-group or authorised inventory-group permissions or the department-owned constraint.
defects.suggested_action: Add a branch or decision for who is allowed to add department-owned inventory assets, and connect it to the add-asset flow.

defects.description: Requirement R12 is not represented with a valid flow in the diagram.
defects.evidence: R12 requires that any faculty member can add all related departments inventory. The add asset section (N18-N27) only models a generic administrator-driven flow and does not include a faculty-member path or related-department scope.
defects.suggested_action: Add a faculty-member add-inventory path that explicitly covers related departments inventory.

defects.description: Requirement R13 is not represented with a valid flow in the diagram.
defects.evidence: R13 requires that any university group member can add all assets in the inventory. The current add-asset sequence does not model university-level authorization for adding all inventory assets; it only shows a generic user/admin flow ending in database update.
defects.suggested_action: Add a university-group member branch that allows adding any asset in the inventory.

defects.description: The diagram adds a 'create new space' and 'modify floor structure' flow directly under the missing asset type branch, but the requirement only authorizes these actions for IT group members after receiving an exception request from any administrative level.
defects.evidence: R18 says IT group members can create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level. In the diagram, N25 is 'Send exception request' and then N26/N27 are performed by '[User]' rather than IT, with no explicit administrative-level trigger to IT.
defects.suggested_action: Relabel and restructure this branch so IT group members perform the space/floor-structure changes only after an exception request from an administrative-level user.

defects.description: The approval flow does not correctly model the required post-approval sequence: notification, waiting-for-execution list, and inventory update on receipt of the asset.
defects.evidence: R20 requires email notification when the request is treated, R21 requires adding the request to the waiting-for-execution list, and R22 requires inventory update when the user receives the requested asset. The diagram shows display pending list -> approve request -> notify user by email, but there is no explicit step for adding the request to the waiting-for-execution list, and inventory update is only shown in a separate return-asset flow (N35-N38), not when the requested asset is received.
defects.suggested_action: Insert a post-approval step to add the request to the waiting-for-execution list and show inventory update on asset receipt in the request workflow.

defects.description: Authentication is not modeled with the required username-and-password input semantics for all users.
defects.evidence: R23 states authentication is made by user name and password for all users. The diagram uses 'Enter credentials' and 'Login' without explicitly showing the username/password authentication step; this is a semantic loss because credentials are not clearly represented as username and password.
defects.suggested_action: Replace or annotate the login input with explicit username and password entry.

defects.description: The permission-change flow is incomplete: it only checks whether the new permissions exceed granted permissions, but it does not explicitly model delegation of another user or acquisition of the inventory administrator role.
defects.evidence: R25 requires an administrative-level user to delegate another user to execute some or all authorized actions, and R26 says the delegated user acquires the role of inventory administrator. The diagram has 'Change permissions', 'Select user', 'Modify permissions', then 'Assign inventory administrator role' after a check, but no explicit delegation action or clear representation that the target user acquires the role as a result of delegation.

defects.description: The add-inventory area does not cover the full set of authorized actors required by the specification. defects.description: The edit-asset flow is not explicit about the required authorization and asset-ownership conditions for the allowed users. review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers many core flows, but it has several semantic and control-flow gaps: request approval/update execution is incomplete, authentication/editing is overgeneralized, some required exception branches are missing, and there are a few unsupported behaviors. Previously noted granularity issues remain but are not repeated unless they still create a semantic defect.

defects.description: The approval flow does not model the required post-approval execution chain: once a request is treated, the user must be notified by email, the request must be added to the waiting-for-execution list, and inventory must be updated when the requested asset is received. The diagram only shows approval and an email step, with no waiting-for-execution state or inventory update tied to asset receipt.
defects.evidence: Requirements state: 'When request is treated, the user is notified by email' (R20), 'The request is added to the waiting for execution list' (R21), and 'Inventory is updated when the user receives the requested asset' (R22). Diagram nodes N39-N41 show display pending request list, approve request, and notify user by email, but there is no node or transition representing addition to the waiting-for-execution list or inventory update on receipt.
defects.suggested_action: Add the missing post-approval steps and connect them in order: approval -> add request to waiting-for-execution list -> notify by email -> execution/receipt event -> inventory update.

defects.description: The edit-asset flow only models a generic search/edit path and a privilege check, but it does not distinguish the required authorized actor classes and ownership constraint. The requirements allow administrative-level users, inventory users, faculty users, and university users to edit assets belonging to their department if authorized; this coverage is not represented explicitly and the privilege gate is attached only after a generic edit path.
defects.evidence: R6-R8 require that different authorized user categories can edit assets belonging to their department. The diagram uses one generic 'Search for asset' -> 'Edit asset' -> 'Modify asset properties' flow with a later 'Sufficient privileges?' decision, but does not represent the required role/department eligibility distinctions or the ownership condition.
defects.suggested_action: Model the authorized editor categories and the 'asset belongs to their department' condition before edit/modification, or otherwise encode the role/ownership checks explicitly in the decision logic.

defects.description: The modification requirement that all fields may be changed except IDs, and that a bulk entry file can be used, is not represented. The diagram only shows a generic 'Modify asset properties' step and no restriction on IDs or bulk-entry path.
defects.evidence: R9 says all fields of an edited asset can be modified except IDs; R10 says a bulk entry file can be used. The diagram contains only 'Modify asset properties' (N12) and 'Fill asset properties' (N23), with no explicit constraint on IDs and no bulk-entry alternative.
defects.suggested_action: Add a modification step that excludes IDs, and include an alternative branch for bulk-entry-file-based modification.

defects.description: The transfer flow does not cover the required approval rules for inter-faculty transfers and transfers outside the university. Inter-faculty transfer approval by faculty group or higher is modeled only as 'create transfer request' and 'approve transfer request' without the stated authority logic; outside-university transfer approval by the university group is shown as a direct approve step but without the explicit approval authority condition.
defects.evidence: R3 requires any authorised user to make inter-faculty transfer requests; R4 requires approval by faculty group or higher; R5 requires transfers outside university to be approved by the university group. The diagram has N58 'Create transfer request', N59 'Approve transfer request', and N60 'Approve transfer', but none of these nodes or decisions encode the required role conditions.
defects.suggested_action: Add explicit role-based approval decisions for inter-faculty and outside-university transfers, with branches for faculty-group-or-higher and university-group approval.

defects.description: The return-asset flow omits the required 'check returned asset and update inventory' behavior by an inventory user. The diagram has only a generic inventory-system check and update path, without the user role performing the check/update as specified.
defects.evidence: R17 requires that an inventory user should check the returned asset and update inventory. The diagram shows 'Check returned asset' and 'Update inventory' in the inventory system lane, not in the inventory user lane, and does not distinguish the user role executing these actions.
defects.suggested_action: Place the returned-asset check/update steps in the inventory-user lane or otherwise explicitly model the inventory user as the actor performing those actions.

defects.description: The exception-request path for creating a new location is incomplete. The requirement says IT group members create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level, but the diagram does not show IT as the actor receiving/processing that exception request, only the user sending it and then directly creating/modifying location structures.
defects.evidence: R18 requires IT group members to create a new space and modify floor structure when they receive an exception request from any administrative level. The diagram shows N25 'Send exception request' and then N26/N27 'Create new space'/'Modify floor structure' in the user lane, with no IT-group receipt or processing step.
defects.suggested_action: Add the IT-group member swimlane actions that receive the exception request and perform the location-creation/floor-structure modification.

defects.description: The diagram introduces an implicit requirement that authentication is only for a specific precondition set, but the requirements only state username/password authentication for all users. The additional linkage of authentication to multiple unrelated preconditions is not supported semantically.
defects.evidence: R23 only requires that authentication is made by user name and password for all users. The decision node N5 is annotated with many unrelated requirement tags (including edit, request, approval, change permissions, and authentication), which implies a broader semantic coupling than the requirement states.
defects.suggested_action: Keep authentication as a standalone username/password login step and avoid implying that it semantically governs unrelated business steps unless those links are explicitly required.

defects.description: The diagram adds an unsupported 'working on waiting for approval / waiting for execution list' condition as a gate for editing, but the requirements only mention this condition for an alternate course in the modify-use-case scenario and do not define it as a general prerequisite for editing assets. Using it as a generic privilege gate changes the meaning of the edit flow.
defects.evidence: R34-R35 describe an alternate course: an administrator or authorised inventory user working on the waiting-for-approval or waiting-for-execution list can edit/modify asset properties. In the diagram, N15 'Sufficient privileges?' is used as a generic gate after editing, which is a different and broader condition than the stated alternate course.
defects.suggested_action: Model the alternate-course condition only where it applies, and do not replace the specified privilege/working-list condition with a generic sufficiency check unless the requirement explicitly says so.

defects.description: The modify-use-case exceptional paths are only partially represented. The diagram shows a no-asset-found error and a generic insufficient-privileges error, but it does not represent the 'asset out of inventory' case as a distinct cause of modification failure.
defects.evidence: R36 requires an error when the asset is out of inventory; R37 requires an error for insufficient privileges; R38 requires an error when no asset is found. The diagram has a decision 'Asset found?' and a generic 'Sufficient privileges?' branch, but no distinct branch for 'asset out of inventory'.
defects.suggested_action: Add a separate decision or exception branch for 'asset out of inventory' so that it is not conflated with general missing-asset or privilege failures.

strengths: The diagram correctly includes the basic authentication flow with success and failure branches.
The same-department direct database update requirement is represented.
The add-new-asset flow includes the main creation steps and the exception path for an unknown type.
The diagram includes search, reporting, permission change, and several approval-related activities.
missing_requirements: Waiting-for-execution list after request approval and inventory update on asset receipt.
Explicit role/ownership constraints for asset editing.
Bulk-entry-file support for editing/modifying assets and adding inventory assets.
Explicit IT-group handling of exception requests for new locations.
Distinct exception branch for asset out of inventory.
Explicit role conditions for inter-faculty and outside-university transfer approvals.

Using user-lane actions for IT-created location changes without an IT actor lane.
Overloading authentication decision with unrelated business-rule requirement tags.
